authorship.contentBindingNote: The proof commits to a content digest but NOTHING WAS CHECKED against it: the payload could not be read here (encrypted to other recipients, absent, or unparseable). Treat this exactly as an unverified content claim — it is neither an attestation of the content nor evidence against it. A digest that WAS checked and failed is reported as `mismatched`, never here.

descriptorBinding.note: the proof names the URN <urn:iep:u-pk-33d42e6b33dc:1792101366182>, so only its terminal segment was matched against the URL — but the pod serving it publishes the same owner the proof signs (<https://identity.interego.xwisee.com/users/u-pk-33d42e6b33dc/profile#me>), so the record is not on some other party's pod. What is still uncompared: the container within that pod, and the pod's ownership claim is the pod's own — nobody signs the pod-to-owner binding.

authorship.signingNote: The relay signed this attestation about the authenticated caller. A separate client signature must be verified to establish authorization by the caller's own key.
